_comment: Constraint Check indicator registry v0.1.2 (prototype; changes from v0.1 and v0.1.1 in docs/CHANGELOG-rubric.md). Fields: id (source code), name, source (worldbank_wdi | worldbank_zip | weo | eci | derived | static), nodes (list of node ids or [] for context), test (price | changes | circumvention | camels | context), class (A|B|C|D|X where X = context, no signal), direction (+1 = higher value means MORE binding, -1 = higher value means LESS binding, 0 = context), transform (none | log1p | log | logit), family (evidence family id; signals within a family are deduplicated to one), slow (true if slow-moving stock: recency decay relaxed), years (first year to ingest), notes. Optional: source_code (World Bank API indicator code when it differs from the id) and source_id (World Bank source/database id) for the bulk-zip fetch; hidden_until_fixed (true = the engine treats the indicator as unavailable: not displayed, not counted); regime_sensitive ("monetary": downgraded to class C for economies in registry/static_monetary_regimes.json, v0.1.2); fallback_for (indicator id: this indicator carries no signal for an economy where that indicator is available in the window, v0.1.2); caveat (one sentence the Desk prints under the indicator).

indicators.name: Proportion of investment financed internally (%)

Higher = firms bypass external finance = more likely binding; ambiguous where firms simply have no profitable projects (read with ES.FIN_NO_NEED).

indicators.name: Percent of firms not needing a loan
indicators.notes: Data360 WB_ES_T_FIN20 (Enterprise Surveys, all sectors). Workbook N0 'Self-financing' row (class B) and reading rule: a high 'did not apply, no need' share puts the country on the low-returns branch. Denominator = firms that did and did not apply. Direction -1: more firms not needing a loan = finance less likely binding.

indicators.name: Percent of firms reporting unfavorable rates, collateral, or procedures as main reason for not applying for loans

Workbook N0 self-financing row, the other half of the 'no need versus terms, collateral or procedures' split: firms that did not apply because rates, collateral or procedures were unfavourable (discouraged borrowers). A behavioural response to the price and terms of credit, so class B on the price test. Despite the BREADY_ prefix it runs 2006-2026. Higher = more binding.

indicators.name: Percent of firms whose recent loan application was rejected

Workbook N0 'Credit rationing' (A/C) and N3 'Firm-level access' (C): share of firms whose recent loan application was rejected. Class C because of the N3 pitfall (firms that expect refusal do not apply, so the rate is selected); the hard rationing measure is IC.FRM.CRDC.FL.ZS. From 2011.

indicators.name: Lending interest rate, nominal (% per year), IMF MFS
indicators.notes: Context input, no signal of its own (class X), placed on N0 and N3 price because it feeds the price of finance: the engine should deflate it exactly like FR.INR.LEND (Fisher, CPI: 100*((1+IMF.LEND/100)/(1+FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG/100)-1)) to extend DERIV.REAL_LENDING_CPI (family real_lending_rate, class A) where WDI lacks the nominal rate. Finding (Oct 2026): WDI FR.INR.LEND is a copy of this IMF series: on all 3,700 shared country-years the values agree to 0.01, and IMF.LEND adds no economy and no year that WDI lacks. It is kept for provenance only; the coverage gain comes from IMF.LEND_EA_NFC (20 EU economies) and IMF.LEND_FC (El Salvador, Cambodia). Coordinator: point the derived real rate at coalesce(FR.INR.LEND, IMF.LEND_EA_NFC, IMF.LEND_FC [dollarized only]) or add a DERIV entry with fallback_for.
indicators.review_note: v0.1.3 coordinator review: identical to WDI FR.INR.LEND; context only

indicators.name: Bank lending rate to non-financial corporations, loans up to 1 year, outstanding amounts (% per year), harmonised euro-area statistics via IMF MFS
indicators.notes: Substitute nominal lending rate for euro-area and other EU reporters that no longer report the IFS lending rate (MFS162), which is why WDI lacks FR.INR.LEND for them. Where both exist (Italy) the two agree closely (2023: 4.91 vs 4.89). Context input (class X) for the CPI-deflated real lending rate, used only where FR.INR.LEND and IMF.LEND are both missing; same family as IMF.LEND.
indicators.caveat: Substitute definition: ECB harmonised MIR rate on short-term corporate loans, not the IFS representative lending rate.
indicators.review_note: v0.1.3 coordinator review: euro-area fallback lending rate; not yet wired into the real-rate derivation (follow-up)

indicators.name: Lending rate on foreign-currency loans (% per year), IMF MFS
indicators.notes: Useful as the lending rate only where most lending is in dollars: El Salvador (officially dollarized) and Cambodia (heavily dollarized). Context input (class X); same family as IMF.LEND.
indicators.caveat: Foreign-currency (mostly US dollar) loans: deflate with US or own CPI only for officially or heavily dollarized economies.
indicators.review_note: v0.1.3 coordinator review: foreign-currency lending rate; only meaningful for dollarized economies; not yet wired (follow-up)

indicators.name: Government bond yield, nominal (% per year), IMF MFS
indicators.notes: Level of the local-currency long-term government yield; input to IMF.GBOND_SPREAD_US. Context only.

indicators.name: Government bond yield spread over US 10-year Treasury (percentage points), proxy for sovereign spread
indicators.notes: PROXY for the Workbook's sovereign spread over US Treasuries (N1 and N10 price, class A), which needs the licensed EMBI. Fills the registry's connectors_not_built family 'sovereign_spreads'. Higher = costlier sovereign borrowing = international finance / macro risk more likely binding (+1). Caveats: local-currency yields embed the inflation and depreciation premium, so high-inflation economies read high even without default risk; coverage is mostly middle and high income economies with a domestic bond market (about 65), and 18 series end in 2017. The coordinator may prefer to class it B or to make it regime_sensitive.
indicators.caveat: Proxy: local-currency government bond yield minus the US 10-year yield, so it includes expected inflation and depreciation as well as default risk; no EMBI licence. Coverage is thin (about 34 economies with 2023+ data).
indicators.review_note: v0.1.3 coordinator review: kept class A so the N10 rule-out family requirement can be met, with an explicit caveat

indicators.name: Gross national savings (% of GDP), WEO
indicators.notes: Same construct as NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS (N2, price test, class C, a quantity: low savings consistent with a savings story, direction -1) and the registry's existing WEO backup NGSD_NGDP (family savings): shares the 'savings' family so it counts once and acts as a backup where WDI is missing. WEO 'actual' data end earlier than 2025 for some economies; the 2025 value can be an estimate.

indicators.name: Total investment / gross capital formation (% of GDP), WEO
indicators.notes: Context, like NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS and the existing WEO backup NID_NGDP (family investment): the investment level used by the top split, not a signal. Backup where WDI is missing.

indicators.name: Nonperforming loans to total gross loans (%), IMF FSI
indicators.notes: Workbook N3 'Non-performing loans and provisioning', FSI, class C. Same source and construct as WDI FB.AST.NPER.ZS (which WDI takes from the IMF FSI), so it shares family 'npl' and counts once; it adds recent years and economies. Higher = weaker loan books (+1).

indicators.name: Bank return on assets (%), IMF FSI
indicators.notes: Workbook N3 'Bank profitability and its durability', class A/B. Proposed B, not A: ROA alone cannot separate protected rents from risk premia (the Workbook needs the P/E of listed banks for that), so high ROA is read as behavior consistent with costly intermediation, not as a price. Higher = more binding (+1). Cross-country accounting differences (FSI metadata) are a further reason not to call it A.

indicators.name: Regulatory capital to risk-weighted assets (%), IMF FSI
indicators.notes: Bank solvency, a quantity (class C, per the brief). Direction -1: thin capital constrains lending; but very high ratios can also mean banks that do not lend, so the signal is weak, and the coordinator may prefer context (X).

indicators.name: Liquid assets to short-term liabilities (%), IMF FSI
indicators.notes: Workbook N0 'Bank liquidity' (liquid assets to deposits; FSI) is listed as class B with a reading rule: liquid banks plus a low real rate point to the low-returns branch. Direction -1 (liquid banks = finance less likely binding). Proposed C rather than B because national definitions of liquid assets and short-term liabilities differ widely (FSI metadata) and levels run from 20% to over 200%, so cross-country ICRs are noisy; promote to B if the coordinator accepts that noise.

indicators.name: Interest margin to gross income (%), IMF FSI
indicators.notes: Share of bank gross income earned from the lending-deposit margin. Related to the Workbook's N3 spread decomposition, but it is an income-mix ratio, not the spread or a margin over assets, so class C. Higher = banks live off the intermediation margin (+1).

indicators.name: Foreign-currency liabilities to total liabilities of deposit takers (%), IMF FSI, dollarization proxy
indicators.notes: Workbook N10 circumvention (deposit dollarization share, class B). The public MFS data carry no foreign-currency deposit split, so this FSI ratio is the proxy; it includes non-deposit FX funding. Fills the connectors_not_built family 'dollarization'. Under formal dollarization (Ecuador, El Salvador, Panama) it reads ~100 by construction: the coordinator should make it regime_sensitive.
indicators.caveat: Proxy for deposit dollarization: includes non-deposit foreign-currency funding.
indicators.review_note: v0.1.3 coordinator review: reads near 100 under formal dollarization; downgraded there like CPI inflation

indicators.name: Foreign-currency loans to total loans of deposit takers (%), IMF FSI, dollarization proxy
indicators.notes: Loan dollarization; same family as IMF.FSI_FX_LIAB (counts once). Workbook N10 circumvention class B. Also regime_sensitive under formal dollarization.
indicators.caveat: Proxy: loan dollarization, not deposit dollarization.
indicators.review_note: v0.1.3 coordinator review: as above

indicators.name: Share of inward direct investment positions held by offshore-centre counterparts (%)
indicators.notes: Workbook N11 property rights circumvention (class B): inward FDI routed through offshore centres (IMF CDIS share from Mauritius, BVI, Netherlands, etc.). Fills the connectors_not_built family 'offshore_fdi'. Higher = more investment structured through jurisdictions offering treaty and legal protection (+1). Offshore list: NLD, LUX, IRL, MUS, VGB, CYM, BMU, CYP, SGP, HKG, CHE, BHS, JEY, GGY, IMN, PAN. Caveat: tax treaty shopping drives the share too, so it is not only a property-rights signal; and it is high in small economies next to a hub.
indicators.caveat: Lower bound: confidential and unreported counterpart cells count as zero.

indicators.name: Trade costs, manufacturing (ISIC D): median over partners (comprehensive trade cost, % ad valorem)
indicators.notes: Workbook N6 first row: bilateral ad valorem trade costs with main partners, class A (a price). High = costlier to trade = transport/logistics more likely binding. Comprehensive cost (tariff included). All twelve ESCAP series share one family so they count once; the coordinator should pick one voter (suggested ESCAP.NTC_TOT_TOP10 or ESCAP.TC_MFG_TOP10) and show the agriculture split per the N6 pitfall. Partly geography (distance, landlocked): ICR should control for landlocked/distance. Latest years (2024-2025) cover fewer pairs. log transform: costs are right-skewed (tens to hundreds of percent).
indicators.review_note: Coordinator review: comprehensive bilateral trade costs include distance and partners' own frictions, so the income-conditional residual also controls for log remoteness; in re-export and accounting hubs (registry/static_trade_hubs.json) output minus exports is a poor proxy for domestic trade, so the measure is class C there (v0.1.5).

indicators.name: Bank overhead costs to total assets (%)
indicators.notes: Mindbook/Workbook N3: the intermediation wedge decomposes as spread = f(reserve requirement eps, operating cost c, deposit rate); the criterion is eps + c. Overhead costs to total assets is the operating-cost term c: a price of intermediation (class A). Higher = costlier intermediation = N3 more likely binding.

indicators.name: Bank net interest margin (%)
indicators.notes: Mindbook/Workbook N3: the intermediation wedge decomposes as spread = f(reserve requirement eps, operating cost c, deposit rate); the criterion is eps + c. Net interest margin is the realized intermediation markup (class A price). Higher = costlier intermediation. Pitfall: high margins are expected when rates are high for savings reasons (N2); read with the deposit rate.

indicators.name: Bank lending-deposit spread
indicators.notes: Lending minus deposit rate (IFS based). Same construct as WDI FR.INR.LNDP, so it is put in the registry's existing 'spread' family to count once; useful where WDI is missing. Class A price; higher = costlier intermediation.

indicators.name: Bank return on assets (%, after tax)
indicators.notes: Bank return on assets after tax. Workbook N3 rates profitability A/B but its reading is ambiguous without P/E ratios (high ROA can be protected rents, i.e. an intermediation markup, or compensation for risk), so proposed class C per the contract's 'when unsure' rule. Direction +1 on the rent reading.

indicators.name: Bank concentration (%)
indicators.notes: Assets of the three largest commercial banks as % of total commercial bank assets. Workbook N3 'Concentration and entry' class C (structure, not a price). Higher = less competition = more likely markup-driven intermediation costs.

indicators.name: Foreign bank assets among total bank assets (%)
indicators.notes: Foreign bank assets as % of total bank assets. Workbook N3 'foreign bank share' class C. Higher = more entry/competition = N3 less likely binding (-1). Series ends around 2013 (Claessens-van Horen bank ownership data).

indicators.name: Foreign banks among total banks (%)
indicators.notes: Foreign banks as % of the number of banks; same family as FOREIGN_ASSETS (asset share preferred).

indicators.name: Bank Z-score
indicators.notes: Bank Z-score (distance to insolvency: (ROA + equity/assets)/sd(ROA)). Class C (a soundness state, not a price); proposed direction -1: a fragile banking system (low Z) makes intermediation riskier and dearer. Weak signal; consider context. log: right-skewed.

indicators.name: Liquid assets to deposits and short term funding (%)
indicators.notes: Liquid assets to deposits and short-term funding. Workbook N0 'Bank liquidity: liquid assets to deposits ... class B': banks hoarding liquidity while investment is low point to low returns, not scarce funds. Higher = finance less likely binding (-1). The test assignment (circumvention) follows the Workbook's class B; the coordinator may prefer 'price' with class C.

indicators.name: Bank credit to bank deposits (%)
indicators.notes: Bank credit to bank deposits. Workbook N0 lists the credit-to-deposit ratio with bank liquidity (class B). High = banks fully lent out relative to their deposit base = loanable funds scarce (+1). Same family as LIQ_DEP (one liquidity construct).

indicators.name: Firm growth tilt against sectors sensitive to access to finance (theta)
indicators.notes: Camels and hippos, firm-level variant (Workbook 4.5): in each Enterprise Survey, the slope of firm employment growth on the sector's sensitivity to access to finance. Negative: exposed sectors grow slower, so the constraint is more likely binding. Sensitivity is measured from the same surveys' obstacle answers, pooled and conditioned on the survey. indicators.name: Hippo gap: absence from finance-dependent products (gamma)
indicators.notes: Camels and hippos (test 4), the presence version: gamma on external finance dependence (Rajan-Zingales). In each year, whether the economy is absent from each scored HS92 4-digit product (RCA within the scored products below 0.2), fitted on log income per product, then each economy's residuals on the product's standardised intensity. Positive gamma: the economy is missing from factor-heavy products more than its income predicts (the hippos are missing), so the factor is more likely binding. This version reads absence, which the growth-based tests cannot see: where a constraint is severe the exposed activities never start. Gates (docs/hippo-gap-test.md): planted-absence power check at s=0.2 (recovery 0.7) and the reliability check (rank correlation of gamma five years apart 0.86 and across the two absence thresholds 0.92, each against a bar of 0.7):  it failed the power gate, so class X (shown, does not vote). Caveats: absence has other causes (comparative advantage, size, nobody tried), so read it with the price and circumvention tests; intensity assumed constant across countries; exports only.
indicators.caveat: Absence has other causes than the constraint: comparative advantage, market size, or that nobody has tried yet.

indicators.notes: Camels and hippos (test 4), the presence version: gamma on schooling intensity (Ciccone-Papaioannou). Positive gamma: the economy is missing from factor-heavy products more than its income predicts (the hippos are missing), so the factor is more likely binding. This version reads absence, which the growth-based tests cannot see: where a constraint is severe the exposed activities never start. Caveats: absence has other causes (comparative advantage, size, nobody tried), so read it with the price and circumvention tests; intensity assumed constant across countries; exports only.

indicators.name: Discovery gap: new competitive exports against those the product space predicts (z)
indicators.notes: The conditional transition count the Workbook's N12 row asks for (ATLAS.TRANSITIONS is the unconditional count): actual new competitive exports over a five-year window minus the number a logistic model predicts from each candidate product's density in the economy's basket, its starting RCA and the economy's income, in binomial standard deviations scaled by the quasi-binomial dispersion and winsorised at +/-4; an entry must reach US$1 million a year. Negative: fewer new products than the economy's position in the product space predicts, the pattern a self-discovery problem leaves (Hausmann and Rodrik 2003), so direction -1. Gates (ingest/productspace.py): placebo centred on zero (passed) and rank correlation across economies between the two windows 0.61 against a bar of 0.5 (passed); both passed, so class B. Caveats: a low gap can also come from a constraint elsewhere (the page's other measures separate the stories); HS4 is coarse; re-exports.
indicators.caveat: Fewer new exports than expected has other causes than under-rewarded discovery: another constraint, re-exports, or a window that caught a shock.

Context: read on the self-discovery page beside the incumbents' survival; low survival points away from self-discovery toward another constraint (H3), so it is not evidence on N12's lean.

indicators.name: World Uncertainty Index (annual mean of quarterly values)
indicators.notes: World Uncertainty Index: the frequency of the word 'uncertainty' (and variants) in the Economist Intelligence Unit country report for the quarter, normalised by the report's total words (file scaling x1,000). Annualised here as the simple mean of the four quarterly values, only for calendar years with all four quarters, so partial years (including the latest, still-incomplete year) are dropped. The raw series is used, not the authors' 3-quarter moving average. It is an academic text-based perception measure of how much uncertainty EIU analysts write about, not a price, a quantity or a firm-reported obstacle, and it moves with global shocks as well as country conditions: class C (informs only). Higher = more uncertainty = more likely binding for policy and macro predictability (Workbook N11). Zero quarters are genuine (no mention), hence log1p.

comovement_specs.notes: If finance binds, investment should fall when real rates rise (Mindbook, Brazil). Wrong sign with high consistency is strong evidence against. v0.1.2: x is a list of candidates; the first with at least min_years pairs is used and recorded as x_source.

Rubric 0.3.1 (10 November 2026): if low domestic savings bind and foreign savings cannot substitute, investment follows domestic saving (Workbook N2 'if binding'; Hausmann, Rodrik and Velasco; Feldstein and Horioka). A rise in gross national saving should be followed by a rise in investment the next year. Lagged one year, like CM.FINANCE and CM.MACRO, so a boom that lifts both in the same year does not read as binding. Saving is measured as a national-accounts residual, so the test reads changes, not levels. Gives N2 its second voting kind of evidence (with the real deposit rate); before it, N2 could not leave 'cannot tell: registry coverage' for any economy.
